# Native preflight discrepancy: e1d470a394ed4761815dd063807d3fa0

Investigation date: 2026-10-28. The live server database was opened read-only for
the job/base records. Its checkout, accepted ledger and rejected job were not changed.
All replay writes belong to the integration-worker-ui worktree.

## Cause

The accepted overlay registered `App/gui/GUI.cpp` with
`#pragma float_control(precise, off)` before `#include "gui/Gui.h"`.
The proposal registered `App/gui/Gui.cpp` separately to remove an assertion.
The old merge retained both dictionary keys. Overlay generation independently
read pristine source for each key; Windows then wrote both to the same file.
The later assertion-only entry replaced the accepted floating-point pragma.

By contrast, native-try edited the already-materialized accepted source, retaining
the pragma. Its local source was therefore different from the independent build.
The rejected materialized GUI source has SHA-256
`f0efba2163086cebc721ffc779138767d000772018753c1440d0c47f8103eddf`.
The native and module flag profile is `/O2 /Ob2 /Oy /GF /GS- /EHsc /MD`,
with VS2008 RTM build 21022. This case establishes a source/pragma discrepancy;
it does not establish a compiler-cache or include-selection defect.

## Frozen comparison

The effective server verification baseline was
`232ae830fd947aadfa731d2add28dcca254150927595ebf3e16183f7b7153e42`.
Its frozen report versus the rejected candidate reports these gains:

`00574b10 00616f60 0062b030 0063c280 00641390 0064e050`

And these losses:

`00573130 00573310 00573770 00573960 00573c00 00573e30 00574050 00574bf0`

The laptop's additional gain, `00641280`, was already owned in this newer server
baseline. Both frozen builds linked and returned smoke-test exit zero. Passing
those checks does not override the linked ownership regression.

## Fixes and diagnostic evidence

Registry merges and guarded replacements use case-insensitive source identity,
preserving accepted spelling. Ambiguous aliases fail before overlay writes.
Saved inputs are archived and cannot be replaced by recheck output. Baseline
changes require revalidation; failed proofs do not discard the original proposals.

Submission now runs the independent snapshot/build/gate implementation locally.
`roc native-try preflight` also runs it without claiming or submitting. The server
still runs its independent proof and every existing acceptance gate.
Receipts retain gained/lost/uncovered addresses and artifact folders. Each freshly
compiled object records command, source hash, include search order, resolved header
hashes and compiler environment in its `.command.json` file. Existing cache tests
cover source/header/compiler changes, flags, include ordering and shadowing.

Local evidence root:
`work/preflight-e1d470/`. It contains the original job/base records, the effective
baseline overlay, the fetched guide revision, and private replay outputs.
The guide was fetched from findings `bfb48043f94cd6cd67aec2cbb8a8ff1c539832a9`
before editing. Worker workflow version 6 includes the shared preflight module.

## Replay validation

The corrected six-file batch was independently recompiled and linked in
`work/preflight-e1d470/corrected-replay/`. Module ownership rose from 3,220 to 3,226:
the six server-relative gains above, with zero losses. The module linked, smoke
returned zero, and all existing acceptance gates passed: M2/M4a/M5, size/base,
linked ownership and global distinct coverage. Global distinct coverage rose to 9,891.
Its `integration-result.json`, `replay-receipt.json` and `integration-*.log` retain
the full reports. All eight previously lost GUI bodies are exact in the fresh object.

The negative control in `work/preflight-e1d470/missing-pragma-replay/` removes only
the accepted FP pragma from that same corrected registry. Its fresh GUI source
hash exactly equals the rejected candidate's hash above. Compiler arguments and
resolved include hashes are identical after normalizing private snapshot paths;
`source-compiler-audit.json` records the comparison. Its fresh GUI object loses
the same eight bodies. The full module links and smoke returns zero, but ownership
falls to 3,218: six gains and eight losses against the frozen baseline.
M2/M4a/M5 also return zero, but the unchanged ownership gate rejects the batch:
`Need new module ownership without losing existing owned bodies`. All eight losses
are uncovered elsewhere; global distinct coverage is 9,883. Its `replay-receipt.json`
records all gained/lost/uncovered addresses and the rejection reason.

Focused regression suite: 244 passed, one optional real-snapshot benchmark skipped.
Worker package verification imports all 47 shipped Python modules, includes the
shared verifier/preflight implementation, and validates ZIP SHA-256 against the
download manifest. The code and package are published without resubmitting this job.

## Remaining limits

No job was submitted or resubmitted; local replay earns no credits. The live server
checkout and database remain unchanged, so server receipt improvements require a
normal code upgrade when the operator can safely do so. The standalone linked
preflight orchestration has regression tests; the real replay exercised its shared
independent build and gate implementation rather than contacting submission APIs.

Cold builds remain expensive. Some unchanged objects also rebuilt across copied
snapshots in this environment; that conservative cache-miss behavior is not fully
diagnosed. Both compared GUI objects were freshly compiled, so it cannot explain
away the controlled pragma regression. There is no evidence here of stale-object
acceptance or a flag/header mismatch causing these eight losses.

Existing limitations remain: two size mismatches, 32 base-probe headers not checked,
and the M4b render milestone not linked. These are unchanged and are not newly
waived checks; this replay does not establish full client runtime compatibility.

# NVIDIA and DeepSeek provider routing investigation

2026-10-28. Source-only fixes; no server database edits or submissions.

## Findings

- Bare `nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b` lost the `nvidia/` API model namespace.
  Explicit `nvidia:nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b` already retained it. Both now
  send the complete model ID. OpenCode uses the separate provider prefix:
  `opencode:nvidia/nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b`.
- Non-transient failures incremented the cloud circuit. Auth-disabled gates then
  reported only a generic open circuit to waiting workers. Gates now retain the
  original safe failure. Only exhausted transient failures count toward a circuit.
  Auth/key/config/model failures stop workers and queued native discovery.
- Installed OpenCode 2.0.16 accepted a positional task, but the old stdin-only CLI
  invocation hung. Native CLI tasks now use a temporary UTF-8 attachment plus an
  explicit instruction, avoiding command-line length limits for large files.
- OpenCode's API generation utility returned empty text for unfenced edit output.
  Native prompts consistently request SEARCH/REPLACE blocks inside a code fence,
  rather than complete C++ files. Unknown HTTP results no longer silently trigger
  a duplicate CLI generation.
- Nemotron Ultra supports `none`, `medium`, `high`, not `low`. Disabled thinking
  now maps to `none` for NVIDIA HTTP and `#none` for OpenCode. Low effort maps to
  medium. Explicit OpenCode variants remain authoritative.

## Validation

- NVIDIA through the contributor's existing OpenCode sign-in: tiny generation
  succeeded in 2.88 seconds. No credential was copied into ROC.
- Real native edit-loop fixture through NVIDIA Nemotron Ultra: 3.7 seconds AI,
  correct anchored edit on its first round. Genuine VS2008 RTM build 21022 COFF
  comparison reproduced one synthetic target and preserved the existing exact
  function. Fixture addresses are synthetic, never client credits. Nothing submitted.
- The contributor's DeepSeek key fetched the model catalog successfully, but
  generation returned HTTP 402 (insufficient balance). The friend's HTTP 401
  cannot be reproduced without that friend's configuration; 401 means credentials
  or access, rather than the balance failure observed here.
- Regression tests cover full IDs, 401/403/404 failure retention without sleeps,
  waiting gate consumers, supported reasoning flags, explicit CLI attachments,
  no duplicate HTTP-to-CLI fallback, and skipping queued files after fatal errors.

The native fixture does not establish gains on the historical client or replace
independent linked ownership/runtime/ABI checks. Remote model latency remains
variable; increasing concurrent requests cannot repair auth, billing or model IDs.

docs/SETUP.md.base:
# Setup and use

Everything runs from one launcher: `roc.cmd` on Windows, `./roc.sh` on Linux. With no
arguments it opens a menu; `roc --help` lists every command, grouped.

## Install

**Windows.** Download the repo (Code → Download ZIP), unzip it, double-click
`install.cmd`. It checks Python 3.12 (installs it with winget if missing), installs
`pefile`, `capstone` and `tzdata`, downloads the exact MSVC compiler bundles, registers
`roconstruct://` links and runs `roc doctor`. It prints download sizes first, needs no
admin rights, and installs no Ollama, Docker or model. Running it again is safe:
downloads resume and `work/`, `src/` and settings are never touched. `roc.cmd` runs it
automatically the first time if setup is missing. The VS2005 and VS2008 RTM bundles
need 7-Zip (`winget install --id 7zip.7zip -e`).

**Linux.** Install Python 3.12+, Wine (`wine wine32` on Debian/Ubuntu) and `cabextract`
or `7z`, then run `./install.sh`. Packages go into a private venv at `tools/venv`;
`./roc.sh` uses it automatically. The old `cl.exe` runs under Wine with a private prefix
in `tools/wineprefix` (your `~/.wine` is untouched). For an emulated Wine loader, set
`ROC_WINE` to its path. `roconstruct://` links and the winget Ollama install are
Windows-only. Linux support adapted from
[brambora69123's fork](https://github.com/brambora69123/RoConstruct).

**Compilers** (`roc install`, checked against a Microsoft signature or known hash):

| Clients | Compiler | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 2008, 2011 | VS2008 RTM 15.00.21022 | [VS2008 Express DVD](https://archive.org/details/VisualStudioExpressEditionsDVD2007) |
| 2009, 2010, 2012 | VS2008 SP1 15.00.30729 | [VCForPython27.msi](https://web.archive.org/web/20210106040224/https://download.microsoft.com/download/7/9/6/796EF2E4-801B-4FC4-AB28-B59FBF6D907B/VCForPython27.msi) |
| 2007 | VS2005 14.00.50727 | [Visual C++ 2005 Express](https://archive.org/details/MS_VisualCPPExpress-2005) |

An existing VS2005/2008 install is found automatically; `ROC_CL` can point at a `cl.exe`.

**Update and uninstall.** `roc update` fast-forwards a git checkout (a ZIP download is
linked to the repository first) and never touches local edits, clients, work, models or
settings. `roc uninstall` lists everything with sizes and asks before each step.

## Start a worker

For a coding-agent-driven session, use [Matching agent](MATCHING_AGENT.md) for
source mining or [Native agent](NATIVE_AGENT.md) for native integration. Both guides
bootstrap a verified Worker download and install missing dependencies when authorized.

Click **Help out** on a client at the
[website](https://colingsnyder2-ux.github.io/RoConstruct/), or run `roc launch`. It asks:
cloud or local model, which model, worker mode (Recommended / Fast / Deep / Advanced /
Optimize), how many workers, and whether to edit advanced options. It then downloads the
client and its compiler if needed, analyzes the binary and runs. Close the window to stop.

Clients download themselves from Google Drive (fallback: `clients.zip`) and are used only
after their SHA-256 matches `clients/clients.json`. `roc client-fetch all` fetches all up
front; `roc client verify` checks a copy you supply at `clients/<name>/<exe>`. Patched exes
are refused (PE checksum). Never commit or share client files.

## Models

| Option | How |
|---|---|
| Cloud API key | `roc provider setup` saves a key (DeepSeek, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, NVIDIA) in a user-local secrets file outside the repo; `roc provider secrets --open` edits it; `roc provider test NAME --model M` sends a two-word probe. Custom providers: `docs/providers.example.json`. |
| ChatGPT plan | `roc chatgpt login` (installs its sign-in packages on first use), pick a model, then `roc launch`. Plus/Pro limits are shared with your other ChatGPT apps; set the app limit at [ChatGPT Settings → Usage](https://chatgpt.com/settings/usage). Tokens are encrypted, the key is held by the OS keyring (Linux: Secret Service or KWallet). `roc chatgpt status`, `models`, `use ID`, `logout`. RoConstruct never falls back to an API key, and a USD cap is rejected for this provider. |
| OpenCode CLI | No key: Match and Agent modes run through the signed-in OpenCode CLI. `npm i -g opencode-ai`, then `opencode auth login`; the dashboard's Install / sign in button does the same. Pick `opencode:…` models from the Match dropdown (or the OpenCode agent CLI) and, if the model supports it, a reasoning variant (`#high`, `#low`, `none`…`max`). `opencode-go/…` models (Go subscription — $80/mo DeepSeek V4.1 Flash allowance) draw on the plan automatically; a USD cap is rejected for them. Model list: `opencode models`. |
| Local model | `roc local-ai` installs Ollama (asks first); `roc local-ai --docker` adds Docker/Rev.ng hints (~5 GB). `roc model` lists and picks models. Local models load the GPU/CPU hard. |
| Claude Code / Codex | Install and sign in to the CLI, then select it under **Workers → Worker / Integrator → Model connection**. Both modes accept CLI models, APIs and local models. See [INTEGRATION.md](INTEGRATION.md). |

Cloud dollar caps need your exact model rates:
`roc provider pricing PROVIDER --model M --input-per-million X --output-per-million Y`.
`roc optimize --model M` calibrates a per-model worker profile on local verified matches
(never submits).

## Dashboard

`roc gui` opens the local dashboard (loopback only; keep its session link private).

- **Workers:** mining workers and native integrators in one chat view with session tabs, loop filters,
  live generated C++, and a configuration drawer. Function workers can pause, resume,
  retune and finish; integration controls apply at file/AI-round boundaries. Worker count controls parallel AI jobs; integration also has a separate compiler cap and batch size.
- **Commands:** run any `roc` command with a preview; jobs queue to protect shared files.
- **Functions / History:** local attempt history (`work/function-history.sqlite`) and saved runs.
- **Servers:** hosting guide, CPU contribution and cluster status (see [SERVER.md](SERVER.md)).
- **Workers → Agent:** choose Claude Code or Codex; install/sign in inside the card.
- **History:** searchable local attempts and server-stored functions; Runs and Experiments expand below.

Closing the tab leaves jobs running; **Exit ROC dashboard** stops them.

## Match by hand

```text
roc next 2008-06              easiest open functions
roc claim 2008-06 006e5040    writes src/2008-06/006e5040.cpp with the target asm as comments
roc check 2008-06 006e5040    compile with the client's compiler: 100% MATCH or a diff
roc classify 2008-06 ADDR F   explain a mismatch
roc submit 2008-06            send sources; the server re-verifies them
roc pull 2008-06              everyone's current sources
```

`ecx` used before it is set means `this`; `ret N` means N bytes of arguments;
`call dword ptr [...]` is an import (`__declspec(dllimport)`); inline asm is rejected;
data your source defines is checked too (wrong data scores 99%).

Automatic passes that need no C++: `roc mass` (all matchers), `roc auto`, `roc libs`
(library recipes), `roc xcopy` (copy matches between clients sharing a compiler),
`roc donor` (RBXGS WebService.dll PDB names), `roc shapes`, `roc research`.

## Where things live

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `roc.py`, `roc/` | the CLI and library |
| `research/` | `recipes.json` experiments, `lessons.json` (ranked lessons), `reports.json` (old report index), `retired.json` (old runners), `repair-patterns.json`, `scout_sources.py` + `artifact-search-log.json` |
| `docs/` | guides and the website |
| `src/` | recovered sources (RoConstruct-findings checkout; ignored here) |
| `work/`, `tools/` | analysis, journals, server DB, compilers, libraries (ignored) |
| `local/` | this PC only: `config/` (settings, providers, worker config), `findings/`, `packages/`, `archive/` |

`packaging/organize-local.ps1` previews (or with `-Apply` performs) moving local state
into `local/`. It never deletes evidence, never deletes the publisher's lock, and skips
anything in use.

## Troubleshooting

`roc doctor` prints every check and the exact fixing command (`--json` for scripts).

| Message | Fix |
|---|---|
| `exe missing` | `roc client-fetch NAME` |
| `hash mismatch` | `roc client remove NAME --purge`, then rerun |
| `looks modified` | get an unmodified exe |
| `missing VS2005 / VS2008` | `roc install` again (resumes) |
| `cannot reach server` | server offline; workers retry |
| `no cloud model key is set` | `roc provider setup`, or `roc local-ai` |
| `worker config was edited` | delete `local/config/roconstruct-worker.json`, run `roc setup` |

# Setup and use

Everything runs from one launcher: `roc.cmd` on Windows, `./roc.sh` on Linux. With no
arguments it opens a menu; `roc --help` lists every command, grouped.

## Install

**Windows.** Download the repo (Code → Download ZIP), unzip it, double-click
`install.cmd`. It checks Python 3.12 (installs it with winget if missing), installs
`pefile`, `capstone` and `tzdata`, downloads the exact MSVC compiler bundles, registers
`roconstruct://` links and runs `roc doctor`. It prints download sizes first, needs no
admin rights, and installs no Ollama, Docker or model. Running it again is safe:
downloads resume and `work/`, `src/` and settings are never touched. `roc.cmd` runs it
automatically the first time if setup is missing. The VS2005 and VS2008 RTM bundles
need 7-Zip (`winget install --id 7zip.7zip -e`).

**Linux.** Install Python 3.12+, Wine (`wine wine32` on Debian/Ubuntu) and `cabextract`
or `7z`, then run `./install.sh`. Packages go into a private venv at `tools/venv`;
`./roc.sh` uses it automatically. The old `cl.exe` runs under Wine with a private prefix
in `tools/wineprefix` (your `~/.wine` is untouched). For an emulated Wine loader, set
`ROC_WINE` to its path. `roconstruct://` links and the winget Ollama install are
Windows-only. Linux support adapted from
[brambora69123's fork](https://github.com/brambora69123/RoConstruct).

**Compilers** (`roc install`, checked against a Microsoft signature or known hash):

| Clients | Compiler | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 2008, 2011 | VS2008 RTM 15.00.21022 | [VS2008 Express DVD](https://archive.org/details/VisualStudioExpressEditionsDVD2007) |
| 2009, 2010, 2012 | VS2008 SP1 15.00.30729 | [VCForPython27.msi](https://web.archive.org/web/20210106040224/https://download.microsoft.com/download/7/9/6/796EF2E4-801B-4FC4-AB28-B59FBF6D907B/VCForPython27.msi) |
| 2007 | VS2005 14.00.50727 | [Visual C++ 2005 Express](https://archive.org/details/MS_VisualCPPExpress-2005) |

An existing VS2005/2008 install is found automatically; `ROC_CL` can point at a `cl.exe`.

**Update and uninstall.** `roc update` fast-forwards a git checkout (a ZIP download is
linked to the repository first) and never touches local edits, clients, work, models or
settings. `roc uninstall` lists everything with sizes and asks before each step.

## Start a worker

For a coding-agent-driven session, use [Matching agent](MATCHING_AGENT.md) for
source mining or [Native agent](NATIVE_AGENT.md) for native integration. Both guides
bootstrap a verified Worker download and install missing dependencies when authorized.

Click **Help out** on a client at the
[website](https://colingsnyder2-ux.github.io/RoConstruct/), or run `roc launch`. It asks:
cloud or local model, which model, worker mode (Recommended / Fast / Deep / Advanced /
Optimize), how many workers, and whether to edit advanced options. It then downloads the
client and its compiler if needed, analyzes the binary and runs. Close the window to stop.

Clients download themselves from Google Drive (fallback: `clients.zip`) and are used only
after their SHA-256 matches `clients/clients.json`. `roc client-fetch all` fetches all up
front; `roc client verify` checks a copy you supply at `clients/<name>/<exe>`. Patched exes
are refused (PE checksum). Never commit or share client files.

## Models

| Option | How |
|---|---|
| Cloud API key | `roc provider setup` saves a key (DeepSeek, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, NVIDIA) in a user-local secrets file outside the repo; `roc provider secrets --open` edits it; `roc provider test NAME --model M` sends a two-word probe. Custom providers: `docs/providers.example.json`. |
| ChatGPT plan | `roc chatgpt login` (installs its sign-in packages on first use), pick a model, then `roc launch`. Plus/Pro limits are shared with your other ChatGPT apps; set the app limit at [ChatGPT Settings → Usage](https://chatgpt.com/settings/usage). Tokens are encrypted, the key is held by the OS keyring (Linux: Secret Service or KWallet). `roc chatgpt status`, `models`, `use ID`, `logout`. RoConstruct never falls back to an API key, and a USD cap is rejected for this provider. |
| OpenCode CLI | No key: Match and Agent modes run through the signed-in OpenCode CLI. `npm i -g opencode-ai`, then `opencode auth login`; the dashboard's Install / sign in button does the same. Pick `opencode:…` models from the Match dropdown (or the OpenCode agent CLI) and, if the model supports it, a reasoning variant (`#high`, `#low`, `none`…`max`). `opencode-go/…` models (Go subscription — $80/mo DeepSeek V4.1 Flash allowance) draw on the plan automatically; a USD cap is rejected for them. Model list: `opencode models`. |
| Local model | `roc local-ai` installs Ollama (asks first); `roc local-ai --docker` adds Docker/Rev.ng hints (~5 GB). `roc model` lists and picks models. Local models load the GPU/CPU hard. |
| Claude Code / Codex | Install and sign in to the CLI, then select it under **Workers → Worker / Integrator → Model connection**. Both modes accept CLI models, APIs and local models. See [INTEGRATION.md](INTEGRATION.md). |

Cloud dollar caps need your exact model rates:
`roc provider pricing PROVIDER --model M --input-per-million X --output-per-million Y`.
`roc optimize --model M` calibrates a per-model worker profile on local verified matches
(never submits).

**OpenRouter:** choose OpenRouter in Worker or Integrator, then save its key in
Settings → Provider credentials (or `roc provider setup`). It uses `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`;
Google models through OpenRouter use this key, not `GEMINI_API_KEY`. The model dropdown
loads OpenRouter's public text-model catalog, cached for five minutes. Manual IDs also
work, including `:free` variants: `openrouter:google/gemini-2.5-flash`. Terminal catalog:
`roc provider models openrouter`. Signed-in OpenCode users can instead select its
`opencode:openrouter/google/...` entry. Reasoning settings use OpenRouter's unified
`reasoning` parameter; mandatory reasoning still depends on the chosen model.

## Dashboard

`roc gui` opens the local dashboard (loopback only; keep its session link private).

- **Workers:** mining workers and native integrators in one chat view with session tabs, loop filters,
  live generated C++, and a configuration drawer. Function workers can pause, resume,
  retune and finish; integration controls apply at file/AI-round boundaries. Worker count controls parallel AI jobs; integration also has a separate compiler cap and batch size.
- **Commands:** run any `roc` command with a preview; jobs queue to protect shared files.
- **Functions / History:** local attempt history (`work/function-history.sqlite`) and saved runs.
- **Servers:** hosting guide, CPU contribution and cluster status (see [SERVER.md](SERVER.md)).
- **Workers → Agent:** choose Claude Code or Codex; install/sign in inside the card.
- **History:** searchable local attempts and server-stored functions; Runs and Experiments expand below.

Closing the tab leaves jobs running; **Exit ROC dashboard** stops them.

## Match by hand

```text
roc next 2008-06              easiest open functions
roc claim 2008-06 006e5040    writes src/2008-06/006e5040.cpp with the target asm as comments
roc check 2008-06 006e5040    compile with the client's compiler: 100% MATCH or a diff
roc classify 2008-06 ADDR F   explain a mismatch
roc submit 2008-06            send sources; the server re-verifies them
roc pull 2008-06              everyone's current sources
```

`ecx` used before it is set means `this`; `ret N` means N bytes of arguments;
`call dword ptr [...]` is an import (`__declspec(dllimport)`); inline asm is rejected;
data your source defines is checked too (wrong data scores 99%).

Automatic passes that need no C++: `roc mass` (all matchers), `roc auto`, `roc libs`
(library recipes), `roc xcopy` (copy matches between clients sharing a compiler),
`roc donor` (RBXGS WebService.dll PDB names), `roc shapes`, `roc research`.

## Where things live

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `roc.py`, `roc/` | the CLI and library |
| `research/` | `recipes.json` experiments, `lessons.json` (ranked lessons), `reports.json` (old report index), `retired.json` (old runners), `repair-patterns.json`, `scout_sources.py` + `artifact-search-log.json` |
| `docs/` | guides and the website |
| `src/` | recovered sources (RoConstruct-findings checkout; ignored here) |
| `work/`, `tools/` | analysis, journals, server DB, compilers, libraries (ignored) |
| `local/` | this PC only: `config/` (settings, providers, worker config), `findings/`, `packages/`, `archive/` |

`packaging/organize-local.ps1` previews (or with `-Apply` performs) moving local state
into `local/`. It never deletes evidence, never deletes the publisher's lock, and skips
anything in use.

## Troubleshooting

`roc doctor` prints every check and the exact fixing command (`--json` for scripts).

| Message | Fix |
|---|---|
| `exe missing` | `roc client-fetch NAME` |
| `hash mismatch` | `roc client remove NAME --purge`, then rerun |
| `looks modified` | get an unmodified exe |
| `missing VS2005 / VS2008` | `roc install` again (resumes) |
| `cannot reach server` | server offline; workers retry |
| `no cloud model key is set` | `roc provider setup`, or `roc local-ai` |
| NVIDIA 404 for Nemotron Ultra | Keep namespace: `nvidia:nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b`. For OpenCode sign-in: `opencode:nvidia/nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b#none`. |
| Cloud HTTP 401/403 | Check key/model access; environment keys override ROC's saved key. OpenCode credentials require an `opencode:` model. |
| DeepSeek HTTP 402 | API balance exhausted; fix billing. Retrying or switching reasoning cannot repair billing. |
| `worker config was edited` | delete `local/config/roconstruct-worker.json`, run `roc setup` |

"""Build the three RoConstruct packages.

    py -3.12 packaging/build.py            # build all three
    py -3.12 packaging/build.py worker     # just one

RoConstruct ships as three zips that share the roc/ package but not the extras:

  RoConstruct Worker   small cloud worker: bootstrap, compilers, worker, no GPU
  RoConstruct Local AI opt-in Ollama/Docker extras, installed over the Worker
  RoConstruct Server   maintainer-only: the group server and website publishing

Each zip is staged, then imported for real before it is packed: a package that
cannot import its own modules is a build failure, not a download problem later.
"""
import ast
import hashlib
import json
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
DIST = ROOT / "local" / "packages"

# Every module a working cloud worker needs (transitive closure of worker, link,
# handoff, doctor, setup, analyze, draft, optimizer and the matchers).
WORKER_MODULES = [
    "telemetry", "agent", "agent_auto", "analyze", "matchers", "chatgpt", "clients", "doctor", "matchers",
    "draft", "fingerprint",
    "tasks", "flags", "gui", "gui_worker", "link", "libs", "match", "mutate",
    "repair", "providers", "refsource", "setup", "setup",
    "worker", "matchers",
]
# Only the maintainer's server needs these, so they stay out of the helper zips.
SERVER_MODULES = ["cluster", "progress", "reports", "server"]
WORKER_MODULES += ["agent_memory", "research", "agent_recovery", "bruteforce", "extents", "remill", "repair_scan", "rtti", "boundaries",
                   "claims", "packet", "scout", "ranking", "routing"]
WORKER_MODULES += ["integration", "integrator", "rebuild", "rebuild_install", "mutsearch", "twinpatch", "native_try", "native_sweep", "standins"]
SERVER_MODULES += ["integration_verify", "integration_notify", "integration_site"]

COMMON_FILES = ["roc.py", "roc.cmd", "roc.sh", "install.cmd", "install.sh",
                "packaging/organize-local.ps1", "research/repair-patterns.json", "docs/SETUP.md", "docs/SERVER.md",
                "research/log.jsonl",
                "CLAUDE.md", "AGENTS.md", "docs/AGENT_GUIDE.md", "research/lessons.json", "research/reports.json",
                "research/recipes.json", "research/template-units.json", "research/function-data.json",
                "README.md", "packaging/requirements-chatgpt.txt", "docs/providers.example.json",
                "roc/web/index.html", "roc/web/style.css", "roc/web/app.js", "roc/web/fonts.css",
                *sorted(p.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix() for p in (ROOT / "roc" / "web" / "fonts").iterdir()),
                "docs/logo.png", "docs/favicon.png",
                "clients/clients.json", "clients/sources.json", "clients/donor.json"]
# Native contributors need trusted recipes/generator, never private vendor trees.
COMMON_FILES += ["docs/INTEGRATION.md", "docs/NATIVE_AGENT.md", "docs/MATCHING_AGENT.md", "research/libs-bundle.json", "research/native-units.json", "research/native-source-lock.json"]
COMMON_FILES += subprocess.check_output(["git", "ls-files", "rebuild/2008-06"],
                                        cwd=ROOT, text=True).splitlines()

PACKAGES = {
    "worker": {
        "name": "RoConstruct Worker",
        "tagline": "Small cloud worker. No GPU, no Ollama, no Docker.",
        "files": COMMON_FILES + [".gitignore"],
        "modules": WORKER_MODULES,
        "docs": {
            "README-FIRST.txt": """RoConstruct Worker
====================

This is the whole helper install. It is deliberately small:

Everything starts from roc.cmd (Linux: ./roc.sh). No arguments opens a menu;
the first run installs what is missing. Models and ChatGPT plan: docs/SETUP.md.

  1. Run install.cmd (Windows) or install.sh (Linux). It checks Python, installs required pip packages
     (pefile, capstone, tzdata), downloads the exact MSVC compiler bundles, registers
     the roconstruct:// link, and opens the website.
  2. Click "Start helping" on the website (or run: roc.cmd launch; Linux: ./roc.sh launch). It asks your
     username, which client, and whether prompts may go to a cloud model.
  3. The worker runs. Cloud models mean your PC stays idle. Only source that
     compiled and matched is uploaded.

Linux needs Wine plus cabextract or 7z. Use ./roc.sh instead of Windows URI links.

Not installed, on purpose: Ollama, Docker, Rev.ng, any local model.
Want a local model later? Install RoConstruct Local AI, or:

    py -3.12 roc.py local-ai

Something wrong? Run:

    py -3.12 roc.py doctor

It prints what is broken and the exact command that fixes it.
""",
        },
    },
    "local-ai": {
        "name": "RoConstruct Local AI",
        "tagline": "Opt-in extras: Ollama for local models, Docker/Rev.ng hints.",
        "files": COMMON_FILES + [".gitignore"],
        "modules": WORKER_MODULES,
        "docs": {
            "README-FIRST.txt": """RoConstruct Local AI
=====================

Unzip this over your RoConstruct Worker install.

Cloud workers (the default) need none of this. Install it only if you want a
local model to run on your own GPU:

    roc.cmd local-ai              install Ollama, then a model
    roc.cmd local-ai --docker     also offer Docker Desktop for Rev.ng hints

Rev.ng is a separate, later step because it costs about 5 GB and needs a restart.
Local models use your GPU and CPU heavily: fans, heat and power draw.
""",
        },
    },
    "server": {
        "name": "RoConstruct Server",
        "tagline": "Maintainer-only: the group server and website publishing.",
        "files": COMMON_FILES + [".gitignore",
                                 "docs/progress.json", "docs/history.json",
                                 ],
        "modules": WORKER_MODULES + SERVER_MODULES,
        "docs": {
            "README-FIRST.txt": """RoConstruct Server (MAINTAINER-ONLY)
==================================

This package is for whoever runs the group server. Helpers do not need it: the
worker packages deliberately leave these modules out, and typing a server
command from a Worker install says so instead of crashing.

    roc.cmd host             start the server (tunnel, publishing, auto-restart)
    py -3.12 roc.py server --help
    py -3.12 roc.py progress          write docs/ for the website
    py -3.12 roc.py server --startup  start `roc host` at logon

Hosting, publishing, private CPU sharing and failover: docs/SERVER.md
    py -3.12 roc.py cluster --help

Do not hand this zip to ordinary helpers.
""",
        },
    },
}


def version():
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"], cwd=ROOT,
                             capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=20)
        return out.stdout.strip() or "dev"
    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
        return "dev"


def stage(slug, spec, out):
    """Copy one package into out/ so it can be imported and zipped."""
    if out.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(out)
    (out / "roc").mkdir(parents=True)
    for relative in spec["files"]:
        source = ROOT / relative
        if not source.is_file():
            raise SystemExit("missing file for %s: %s" % (slug, relative))
        target = out / relative
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copyfile(source, target)
    # Adopted headers are compiler inputs even if no ordinary mined snippet named them.
    overlay = ROOT / 'rebuild/2008-06/patches/rbxgs-client.json'
    native = json.loads((ROOT / 'research/native-units.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
    adopted = {}
    for edits in json.loads(overlay.read_text(encoding='utf-8')).values():
        for old, ref in edits:
            if old != '@replace':
                continue
            relative = Path(ref)
            if relative.parts[0] != 'App' or '..' in relative.parts or not relative.name.startswith('roc_'):
                raise SystemExit('Unsupported native dependency: ' + ref)
            name = Path(*relative.parts[1:]).as_posix()
            path = ROOT / 'tools/rbxgs/Client' / relative
            text = path.read_text(errors='replace') if path.exists() else native.get('../rbxgs/Client/App', {}).get(name)
            if text is None:
                raise SystemExit('Missing native dependency: ' + ref)
            adopted[name] = text
    (out / 'research/native-units.json').write_text(json.dumps(
        {'../rbxgs/Client/App': adopted}, indent=1, sort_keys=True) + '\n', encoding='utf-8')
    for module in spec["modules"]:
        source = ROOT / "roc" / ("%s.py" % module)
        if not source.is_file():
            raise SystemExit("missing module for %s: roc/%s.py" % (slug, module))
        shutil.copyfile(source, out / "roc" / source.name)
    shutil.copytree(ROOT / "roc" / "web", out / "roc" / "web", dirs_exist_ok=True)
    (out / "roc" / "__init__.py").write_text("", encoding="utf-8")
    (out / "roconstruct-package.json").write_text(json.dumps(
        {"package": slug, "revision": version(), "native_workflow": True, "native_workflow_version": 5,
         "matching_workflow_version": 1}, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    for name, text in spec["docs"].items():
        (out / name).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    return out


def referenced_modules(staged):
    """Every roc.* module roc.py mentions, at any depth."""
    tree = ast.parse((staged / "roc.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    names = set()
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and node.module and node.module.startswith("roc."):
            names.add(node.module.split(".", 1)[1])
        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and node.module == "roc":
            # from roc import draft, worker
            names.update(alias.name for alias in node.names if alias.name != "worker")
        elif isinstance(node, ast.Import):
            for alias in node.names:
                if alias.name.startswith("roc."):
                    names.add(alias.name.split(".", 1)[1])
        elif isinstance(node, ast.Call) and getattr(node.func, "id", "") == "need_module":
            # need_module("server", ...) is how a package leaves a module out on purpose.
            if node.args and isinstance(node.args[0], ast.Constant) and isinstance(node.args[0].value, str):
                names.add(node.args[0].value)
        elif isinstance(node, ast.Call) and getattr(node.func, "id", "") == "__import__":
            if node.args and isinstance(node.args[0], ast.Constant) and isinstance(node.args[0].value, str):
                module = node.args[0].value
                if module.startswith("roc."):
                    names.add(module.split(".", 1)[1])
    return names


def audit(staged, spec):
    """Fail the build when roc.py needs a module this package leaves out.

    Every roc import in roc.py sits inside a command, so a left-out module only
    breaks that one command. It is allowed for exactly the maintainer modules,
    which roc.py reaches through need_module() and reports as such.
    """
    left_out = sorted(name for name in referenced_modules(staged)
                      if name not in spec["modules"] and name != "worker")
    unexpected = [name for name in left_out if name not in SERVER_MODULES]
    if unexpected:
        raise SystemExit("these modules are referenced by roc.py but missing from the %s package: %s"
                         % (spec["name"], ", ".join(unexpected)))
    return left_out


def verify(staged):
    """Import every module in the staged tree, from that tree, with the repo off the path."""
    modules = sorted(p.stem for p in (staged / "roc").glob("*.py") if p.stem != "__init__")
    code = "import importlib,sys\n" \
           "for name in %r:\n    importlib.import_module('roc.' + name)\n" \
           "import ast\n" \
           "ast.parse(open('roc.py', encoding='utf-8').read())\n" \
           "print('imported', len(%r), 'modules')\n" % (modules, modules)
    run = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", code], cwd=staged, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if run.returncode:
        raise SystemExit("package does not import:\n%s" % (run.stderr.strip() or run.stdout.strip()))
    return run.stdout.strip()


def pack(staged, target):
    with zipfile.ZipFile(target, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zf:
        for path in sorted(staged.rglob("*")):
            if path.is_file():
                zf.write(path, path.relative_to(staged).as_posix())
    return target


def build(slug):
    spec = PACKAGES[slug]
    staged = DIST / ("stage-" + slug)
    stage(slug, spec, staged)
    leaks = audit(staged, spec)
    print("  modules: %d" % len(spec["modules"]))
    print("  maintainer modules left out: %s" % (", ".join(leaks) or "none"))
    print("  check: %s" % verify(staged))
    target = pack(staged, DIST / ("%s-%s.zip" % (slug, version())))
    print("  %s (%.1f KB)" % (target.name, target.stat().st_size / 1024))
    return target


def main(argv):
    wanted = argv or list(PACKAGES)
    unknown = [slug for slug in wanted if slug not in PACKAGES]
    if unknown:
        raise SystemExit("unknown package(s): %s. Choose from: %s" % (", ".join(unknown), ", ".join(PACKAGES)))
    DIST.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    print("RoConstruct packages (version %s)" % version())
    for slug in wanted:
        print("\n%s" % PACKAGES[slug]["name"])
        print("  %s" % PACKAGES[slug]["tagline"])
        target = build(slug)
        if slug == "worker":
            prepare_downloads(target)
    print("\nWrote %s" % DIST)
    print("A helper only needs RoConstruct Worker. Local AI and Server are opt-in.")


def prepare_downloads(package):
    """Refresh the shared bootstrap ZIP/manifest and both standalone agent guides."""
    with zipfile.ZipFile(package) as zipped:
        marker = json.loads(zipped.read("roconstruct-package.json"))
        if marker.get("matching_workflow_version", 0) < 1 or not {
                "docs/MATCHING_AGENT.md", "docs/NATIVE_AGENT.md"} <= set(zipped.namelist()):
            raise ValueError("Worker ZIP lacks the matching/native workflows; rebuild it")
    folder = ROOT / "local/findings/data"
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    manifest = folder / "native-worker.json"
    data = json.loads(manifest.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if manifest.exists() else {}
    base = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/colingsnyder2-ux/RoConstruct-findings/main/data/"
    archive = folder / "native-worker.zip"
    shutil.copy2(package, archive)
    for name in ("NATIVE_AGENT.md", "MATCHING_AGENT.md"):
        shutil.copy2(ROOT / "docs" / name, folder / name)
    data.update(schema=1, workflow_version=5, matching_workflow_version=1,
                url=base + archive.name, sha256=hashlib.sha256(archive.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
                size=archive.stat().st_size, guide=base + "NATIVE_AGENT.md", matching_guide=base + "MATCHING_AGENT.md",
                native_clients=["2008-06"], invitation_required=False)
    data.setdefault("server", "https://colinpc.tail2879d0.ts.net")
    data.setdefault("status_url", data["server"].rstrip("/") + "/v1/status")

"""Build the three RoConstruct packages.

    py -3.12 packaging/build.py            # build all three
    py -3.12 packaging/build.py worker     # just one

RoConstruct ships as three zips that share the roc/ package but not the extras:

  RoConstruct Worker   small cloud worker: bootstrap, compilers, worker, no GPU
  RoConstruct Local AI opt-in Ollama/Docker extras, installed over the Worker
  RoConstruct Server   maintainer-only: the group server and website publishing

Each zip is staged, then imported for real before it is packed: a package that
cannot import its own modules is a build failure, not a download problem later.
"""
import ast
import hashlib
import json
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
DIST = ROOT / "local" / "packages"

# Every module a working cloud worker needs (transitive closure of worker, link,
# handoff, doctor, setup, analyze, draft, optimizer and the matchers).
WORKER_MODULES = [
    "telemetry", "agent", "agent_auto", "analyze", "matchers", "chatgpt", "clients", "doctor", "matchers",
    "draft", "fingerprint",
    "tasks", "flags", "gui", "gui_worker", "link", "libs", "match", "mutate",
    "repair", "providers", "refsource", "setup", "setup",
    "worker", "matchers",
]
# Only the maintainer's server needs these, so they stay out of the helper zips.
SERVER_MODULES = ["cluster", "progress", "reports", "server"]
WORKER_MODULES += ["agent_memory", "research", "agent_recovery", "bruteforce", "extents", "remill", "repair_scan", "rtti", "boundaries",
                   "claims", "packet", "scout", "ranking", "routing"]
WORKER_MODULES += ["integration", "integrator", "rebuild", "rebuild_install", "mutsearch", "twinpatch", "native_try", "native_sweep", "native_batch", "standins"]
WORKER_MODULES += ["integration_verify"]  # contributor linked preflight shares authoritative build/gates
SERVER_MODULES += ["integration_notify", "integration_site"]

COMMON_FILES = ["roc.py", "roc.cmd", "roc.sh", "install.cmd", "install.sh",
                "packaging/organize-local.ps1", "research/repair-patterns.json", "docs/SETUP.md", "docs/SERVER.md",
                "research/log.jsonl",
                "CLAUDE.md", "AGENTS.md", "docs/AGENT_GUIDE.md", "research/lessons.json", "research/reports.json",
                "research/recipes.json", "research/template-units.json", "research/function-data.json",
                "README.md", "packaging/requirements-chatgpt.txt", "docs/providers.example.json",
                "roc/web/index.html", "roc/web/style.css", "roc/web/app.js", "roc/web/fonts.css",
                *sorted(p.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix() for p in (ROOT / "roc" / "web" / "fonts").iterdir()),
                "docs/logo.png", "docs/favicon.png",
                "clients/clients.json", "clients/sources.json", "clients/donor.json"]
# Native contributors need trusted recipes/generator, never private vendor trees.
COMMON_FILES += ["docs/INTEGRATION.md", "docs/INTEGRATOR_PERFORMANCE.md", "benchmarks/native_compile_batches.py", "benchmarks/native_matcher.py", "docs/NATIVE_AGENT.md", "docs/MATCHING_AGENT.md", "research/libs-bundle.json", "research/native-units.json", "research/native-source-lock.json"]
COMMON_FILES += subprocess.check_output(["git", "ls-files", "rebuild/2008-06"],
                                        cwd=ROOT, text=True).splitlines()

PACKAGES = {
    "worker": {
        "name": "RoConstruct Worker",
        "tagline": "Small cloud worker. No GPU, no Ollama, no Docker.",
        "files": COMMON_FILES + [".gitignore"],
        "modules": WORKER_MODULES,
        "docs": {
            "README-FIRST.txt": """RoConstruct Worker
====================

This is the whole helper install. It is deliberately small:

Everything starts from roc.cmd (Linux: ./roc.sh). No arguments opens a menu;
the first run installs what is missing. Models and ChatGPT plan: docs/SETUP.md.

  1. Run install.cmd (Windows) or install.sh (Linux). It checks Python, installs required pip packages
     (pefile, capstone, tzdata), downloads the exact MSVC compiler bundles, registers
     the roconstruct:// link, and opens the website.
  2. Click "Start helping" on the website (or run: roc.cmd launch; Linux: ./roc.sh launch). It asks your
     username, which client, and whether prompts may go to a cloud model.
  3. The worker runs. Cloud models mean your PC stays idle. Only source that
     compiled and matched is uploaded.

Linux needs Wine plus cabextract or 7z. Use ./roc.sh instead of Windows URI links.

Not installed, on purpose: Ollama, Docker, Rev.ng, any local model.
Want a local model later? Install RoConstruct Local AI, or:

    py -3.12 roc.py local-ai

Something wrong? Run:

    py -3.12 roc.py doctor

It prints what is broken and the exact command that fixes it.
""",
        },
    },
    "local-ai": {
        "name": "RoConstruct Local AI",
        "tagline": "Opt-in extras: Ollama for local models, Docker/Rev.ng hints.",
        "files": COMMON_FILES + [".gitignore"],
        "modules": WORKER_MODULES,
        "docs": {
            "README-FIRST.txt": """RoConstruct Local AI
=====================

Unzip this over your RoConstruct Worker install.

Cloud workers (the default) need none of this. Install it only if you want a
local model to run on your own GPU:

    roc.cmd local-ai              install Ollama, then a model
    roc.cmd local-ai --docker     also offer Docker Desktop for Rev.ng hints

Rev.ng is a separate, later step because it costs about 5 GB and needs a restart.
Local models use your GPU and CPU heavily: fans, heat and power draw.
""",
        },
    },
    "server": {
        "name": "RoConstruct Server",
        "tagline": "Maintainer-only: the group server and website publishing.",
        "files": COMMON_FILES + [".gitignore",
                                 "docs/progress.json", "docs/history.json",
                                 ],
        "modules": WORKER_MODULES + SERVER_MODULES,
        "docs": {
            "README-FIRST.txt": """RoConstruct Server (MAINTAINER-ONLY)
==================================

This package is for whoever runs the group server. Helpers do not need it: the
worker packages deliberately leave these modules out, and typing a server
command from a Worker install says so instead of crashing.

    roc.cmd host             start the server (tunnel, publishing, auto-restart)
    py -3.12 roc.py server --help
    py -3.12 roc.py progress          write docs/ for the website
    py -3.12 roc.py server --startup  start `roc host` at logon

Hosting, publishing, private CPU sharing and failover: docs/SERVER.md
    py -3.12 roc.py cluster --help

Do not hand this zip to ordinary helpers.
""",
        },
    },
}


def version():
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"], cwd=ROOT,
                             capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=20)
        return out.stdout.strip() or "dev"
    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
        return "dev"


def stage(slug, spec, out):
    """Copy one package into out/ so it can be imported and zipped."""
    from roc.rebuild_install import ensure_abi
    abi = ensure_abi(ROOT)
    if out.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(out)
    (out / "roc").mkdir(parents=True)
    for relative in spec["files"]:
        source = ROOT / relative
        if not source.is_file():
            raise SystemExit("missing file for %s: %s" % (slug, relative))
        target = out / relative
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copyfile(source, target)
    target = out / 'rebuild/2008-06/manifests/abi-evidence.json'
    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copyfile(abi, target)
    # Adopted headers are compiler inputs even if no ordinary mined snippet named them.
    overlay = ROOT / 'rebuild/2008-06/patches/rbxgs-client.json'
    native = json.loads((ROOT / 'research/native-units.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
    adopted = {}
    for edits in json.loads(overlay.read_text(encoding='utf-8')).values():
        for old, ref in edits:
            if old != '@replace':
                continue
            relative = Path(ref)
            if relative.parts[0] != 'App' or '..' in relative.parts or not relative.name.startswith('roc_'):
                raise SystemExit('Unsupported native dependency: ' + ref)
            name = Path(*relative.parts[1:]).as_posix()
            path = ROOT / 'tools/rbxgs/Client' / relative
            text = path.read_text(errors='replace') if path.exists() else native.get('../rbxgs/Client/App', {}).get(name)
            if text is None:
                raise SystemExit('Missing native dependency: ' + ref)
            adopted[name] = text
    (out / 'research/native-units.json').write_text(json.dumps(
        {'../rbxgs/Client/App': adopted}, indent=1, sort_keys=True) + '\n', encoding='utf-8')
    for module in spec["modules"]:
        source = ROOT / "roc" / ("%s.py" % module)
        if not source.is_file():
            raise SystemExit("missing module for %s: roc/%s.py" % (slug, module))
        shutil.copyfile(source, out / "roc" / source.name)
    shutil.copytree(ROOT / "roc" / "web", out / "roc" / "web", dirs_exist_ok=True)
    (out / "roc" / "__init__.py").write_text("", encoding="utf-8")
    (out / "roconstruct-package.json").write_text(json.dumps(
        {"package": slug, "revision": version(), "native_workflow": True, "native_workflow_version": 12,
         "matching_workflow_version": 4}, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    for name, text in spec["docs"].items():
        (out / name).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    return out


def referenced_modules(staged):
    """Every roc.* module roc.py mentions, at any depth."""
    tree = ast.parse((staged / "roc.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    names = set()
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and node.module and node.module.startswith("roc."):
            names.add(node.module.split(".", 1)[1])
        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and node.module == "roc":
            # from roc import draft, worker
            names.update(alias.name for alias in node.names if alias.name != "worker")
        elif isinstance(node, ast.Import):
            for alias in node.names:
                if alias.name.startswith("roc."):
                    names.add(alias.name.split(".", 1)[1])
        elif isinstance(node, ast.Call) and getattr(node.func, "id", "") == "need_module":
            # need_module("server", ...) is how a package leaves a module out on purpose.
            if node.args and isinstance(node.args[0], ast.Constant) and isinstance(node.args[0].value, str):
                names.add(node.args[0].value)
        elif isinstance(node, ast.Call) and getattr(node.func, "id", "") == "__import__":
            if node.args and isinstance(node.args[0], ast.Constant) and isinstance(node.args[0].value, str):
                module = node.args[0].value
                if module.startswith("roc."):
                    names.add(module.split(".", 1)[1])
    return names


def audit(staged, spec):
    """Fail the build when roc.py needs a module this package leaves out.

    Every roc import in roc.py sits inside a command, so a left-out module only
    breaks that one command. It is allowed for exactly the maintainer modules,
    which roc.py reaches through need_module() and reports as such.
    """
    left_out = sorted(name for name in referenced_modules(staged)
                      if name not in spec["modules"] and name != "worker")
    unexpected = [name for name in left_out if name not in SERVER_MODULES]
    if unexpected:
        raise SystemExit("these modules are referenced by roc.py but missing from the %s package: %s"
                         % (spec["name"], ", ".join(unexpected)))
    return left_out


def verify(staged):
    """Import every module in the staged tree, from that tree, with the repo off the path."""
    modules = sorted(p.stem for p in (staged / "roc").glob("*.py") if p.stem != "__init__")
    code = "import importlib,sys\n" \
           "for name in %r:\n    importlib.import_module('roc.' + name)\n" \
           "import ast\n" \
           "ast.parse(open('roc.py', encoding='utf-8').read())\n" \
           "print('imported', len(%r), 'modules')\n" % (modules, modules)
    run = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", code], cwd=staged, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if run.returncode:
        raise SystemExit("package does not import:\n%s" % (run.stderr.strip() or run.stdout.strip()))
    return run.stdout.strip()


def pack(staged, target):
    with zipfile.ZipFile(target, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zf:
        for path in sorted(staged.rglob("*")):
            if path.is_file():
                zf.write(path, path.relative_to(staged).as_posix())
    return target


def build(slug):
    spec = PACKAGES[slug]
    staged = DIST / ("stage-" + slug)
    stage(slug, spec, staged)
    leaks = audit(staged, spec)
    print("  modules: %d" % len(spec["modules"]))
    print("  maintainer modules left out: %s" % (", ".join(leaks) or "none"))
    print("  check: %s" % verify(staged))
    target = pack(staged, DIST / ("%s-%s.zip" % (slug, version())))
    print("  %s (%.1f KB)" % (target.name, target.stat().st_size / 1024))
    return target


def main(argv):
    wanted = argv or list(PACKAGES)
    unknown = [slug for slug in wanted if slug not in PACKAGES]
    if unknown:
        raise SystemExit("unknown package(s): %s. Choose from: %s" % (", ".join(unknown), ", ".join(PACKAGES)))
    DIST.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    print("RoConstruct packages (version %s)" % version())
    for slug in wanted:
        print("\n%s" % PACKAGES[slug]["name"])
        print("  %s" % PACKAGES[slug]["tagline"])
        target = build(slug)
        if slug == "worker":
            prepare_downloads(target)
    print("\nWrote %s" % DIST)
    print("A helper only needs RoConstruct Worker. Local AI and Server are opt-in.")


def prepare_downloads(package):
    """Refresh the shared bootstrap ZIP/manifest and both standalone agent guides."""
    with zipfile.ZipFile(package) as zipped:
        marker = json.loads(zipped.read("roconstruct-package.json"))
        if marker.get("matching_workflow_version", 0) < 4 or not {
                "docs/MATCHING_AGENT.md", "docs/NATIVE_AGENT.md",
                "rebuild/2008-06/manifests/abi-evidence.json"} <= set(zipped.namelist()):
            raise ValueError("Worker ZIP lacks the matching/native workflows; rebuild it")
        abi = zipped.read('rebuild/2008-06/manifests/abi-evidence.json')
    folder = ROOT / "local/findings/data"
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    manifest = folder / "native-worker.json"
    data = json.loads(manifest.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if manifest.exists() else {}
    base = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/colingsnyder2-ux/RoConstruct-findings/main/data/"
    archive = folder / "native-worker.zip"
    shutil.copy2(package, archive)
    for name in ("NATIVE_AGENT.md", "MATCHING_AGENT.md"):
        shutil.copy2(ROOT / "docs" / name, folder / name)
    data.update(schema=1, workflow_version=12, matching_workflow_version=4,
                abi_manifest_sha256=hashlib.sha256(abi).hexdigest(), abi_manifest_classes=len(json.loads(abi)),
                url=base + archive.name, sha256=hashlib.sha256(archive.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
                size=archive.stat().st_size, guide=base + "NATIVE_AGENT.md", matching_guide=base + "MATCHING_AGENT.md",
                native_clients=["2008-06"], invitation_required=False)
    data.setdefault("server", "https://colinpc.tail2879d0.ts.net")
    data.setdefault("status_url", data["server"].rstrip("/") + "/v1/status")
    manifest.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print("  Bootstrap ZIP + matching/native guides refreshed: %s" % folder)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1:])

"""Findings Git transport shared by server and independent hourly publisher."""
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import tempfile
import uuid


def publish_downloads(root, git_exe, log=print):
    """Publish only reviewed native Worker assets, preserving the remote findings tree."""
    root = Path(root)
    folder = root / 'local/findings/data'
    files = ['native-worker.zip', 'native-worker.json', 'NATIVE_AGENT.md', 'MATCHING_AGENT.md']
    manifest = json.loads((folder / 'native-worker.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
    if hashlib.sha256((folder / 'native-worker.zip').read_bytes()).hexdigest() != manifest['sha256']:
        raise ValueError('Worker download hash mismatch; rebuild the download bundle')
    index = root / 'work' / ('downloads-index-' + uuid.uuid4().hex)
    index.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    env = dict(os.environ, GIT_INDEX_FILE=str(index))
    def git(*args):
        result = subprocess.run([git_exe, *args], cwd=root, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
        if result.returncode:
            raise RuntimeError('Download publication failed: ' + result.stderr.strip()[-300:])
        return result.stdout.strip()
    try:
        git('fetch', 'findings', 'refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/findings/main')
        parent = git('rev-parse', 'refs/remotes/findings/main')
        git('read-tree', parent)
        for name in files:
            blob = git('hash-object', '-w', '--', str(folder / name))
            git('update-index', '--add', '--cacheinfo', '100644', blob, 'data/' + name)
        tree = git('write-tree')
        if tree == git('rev-parse', parent + '^{tree}'):
            return log('Native Worker download already current.')
        commit = git('commit-tree', tree, '-p', parent, '-m', 'Publish native Worker download')
        git('push', 'findings', commit + ':refs/heads/main')
        log('Native Worker download published: ' + commit)
    finally:
        index.unlink(missing_ok=True)


def publish_package(root, git_exe, log=print):
    """Update the native package using existing blobs for unchanged or renamed files."""
    root = Path(root)
    folder = root / 'local/findings/2008-06'
    manifest = json.loads((folder / 'package.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
    index = root / 'work' / ('package-index-' + uuid.uuid4().hex)
    index.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    env = dict(os.environ, GIT_INDEX_FILE=str(index))
    def git(*args, **kwargs):
        result = subprocess.run([git_exe, *args], cwd=root, env=env, capture_output=True,
                                text=True, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace', timeout=120, **kwargs)
        if result.returncode:
            raise RuntimeError('Package publication failed: ' + result.stderr.strip()[-300:])
        return result.stdout.strip()
    try:
        git('fetch', 'findings', 'refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/findings/main')
        parent = git('rev-parse', 'refs/remotes/findings/main')
        previous = json.loads(git('show', parent + ':2008-06/package.json'))
        git('read-tree', parent)
        blobs = {}
        for row in git('ls-tree', '-r', '-z', parent, '--', '2008-06').split('\0'):
            if row:
                meta, path = row.split('\t', 1)
                blobs[path] = meta.split()[2]
        rows = ['0 ' + '0' * 40 + '\t2008-06/' + path + '\0'
                for path in previous['files'].keys() - manifest['files'].keys()]
        for relative in [*manifest['files'], 'package.json']:
            old = relative
            if old not in previous['files'] and relative.startswith('src/Client/'):
                old = relative.replace('src/Client/', 'src/rbxgs/Client/', 1)
            same = relative != 'package.json' and manifest['files'][relative] == previous['files'].get(old)
            blob = blobs.get('2008-06/' + old) if same else None
            if not blob:
                blob = git('hash-object', '-w', '--', str(folder / relative))
            rows.append('100644 ' + blob + '\t2008-06/' + relative + '\0')
        git('update-index', '-z', '--index-info', input=''.join(rows))
        tree = git('write-tree')
        if tree == git('rev-parse', parent + '^{tree}'):
            return log('Native package already current.')
        commit = git('commit-tree', tree, '-p', parent, '-m', 'Flatten native Client source path')
        git('push', 'findings', commit + ':refs/heads/main')
        log('Native package published: ' + commit)
    finally:
        index.unlink(missing_ok=True)


def publish(root, git_exe, log=print):
    """Copy local recovered sources into the separate findings repository."""
    from roc.server import findings_source
    source = root / "src"
    if not source.exists():
        return
    index = root / "work" / ("findings-index-" + uuid.uuid4().hex)
    index.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    env = os.environ.copy()
    env["GIT_INDEX_FILE"] = str(index)
    git = lambda *a: subprocess.run([git_exe, *a], cwd=root, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)
    try:
        fetched = git("fetch", "findings", "main")
        if fetched.returncode:
            return log("Findings fetch failed: %s" % fetched.stderr.strip()[-300:])
        parent = git("rev-parse", "FETCH_HEAD")
        if parent.returncode:
            return log("Findings revision unavailable: %s" % parent.stderr.strip()[-300:])
        parent = parent.stdout.strip()
        # The findings tree is rebuilt from an allowlist (sources + portable evidence), so files
        # that do not belong there never persist. sync_findings has already exported every
        # stored source into src/.
        if git("read-tree", "--empty").returncode or git("add", "-f", "src").returncode:
            return log("Findings source staging failed.")
        from roc import libs
        units = libs.generated_units()
        # Stream blobs into one Git pack; avoid a temporary file/process per function.
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="findings-sources-", dir=root / "work") as temporary:
            names, seen = [], {}
            marks = Path(temporary) / "marks"
            listed = git("ls-files", "--stage", "-z", "--", "src")
            if listed.returncode:
                return log("Findings source listing failed.")
            rows = [row.split("\t", 1) for row in listed.stdout.split("\0") if row]
            with tempfile.TemporaryFile(dir=temporary) as originals, tempfile.TemporaryFile(dir=temporary) as stream:
                # Reading staged blobs in bulk avoids reopening 170k files on Windows.
                read = subprocess.run([git_exe, "cat-file", "--batch"], cwd=root, env=env,
                    input=("\n".join(meta.split()[1] for meta, _ in rows) + "\n").encode(),
                    stdout=originals, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
                if read.returncode:
                    return log("Findings source reading failed: " + read.stderr.decode(errors="replace")[-300:])
                originals.seek(0)
                for _, relative in rows:
                    size = int(originals.readline().split()[-1])
                    text = originals.read(size).decode("utf-8", errors="replace").replace("\r\n", "\n")
                    originals.read(1)  # batch record separator
                    expanded = findings_source(text, units)
                    if expanded == text:
                        continue
                    body = expanded.encode("utf-8")
                    digest = hashlib.sha256(body).digest()
                    if digest not in seen:
                        seen[digest] = len(seen) + 1
                        stream.write(("blob\nmark :%d\ndata %d\n" % (seen[digest], len(body))).encode("ascii"))
                        stream.write(body)
                        stream.write(b"\n")
                    names.append((relative, seen[digest]))
                stream.write(b"done\n")
                stream.seek(0)
                if names:
                    blobs = subprocess.run([git_exe, "fast-import", "--quiet", "--done", "--export-marks=" + str(marks)],
                                           cwd=root, env=env, stdin=stream, capture_output=True, text=True)
                    if blobs.returncode:
                        return log("Findings source hashing failed: " + blobs.stderr.strip()[-300:])
            if names:
                hashes = dict(line.split() for line in marks.read_text().splitlines())
                staged = subprocess.run([git_exe, "update-index", "-z", "--index-info"], cwd=root, env=env,
                                        input="".join("100644 %s\t%s\0" % (hashes[":" + str(mark)], name)
                                                      for name, mark in names),
                                        capture_output=True, text=True)
                if staged.returncode:
                    return log("Findings source staging failed: " + staged.stderr.strip()[-300:])
                log("Prepared %d readable library sources." % len(names))
        findings = root / 'local/findings'
        portable = [findings / 'README.md', findings / '.gitignore',
                    findings / 'agent-memory/lessons.json',
                    *[path for folder in ('.github', 'units', 'data')
                      for path in sorted((findings / folder).rglob('*'))]]
        package = findings / '2008-06'
        package_index = package / 'package.json'
        if package_index.is_file():
            portable.append(package_index)
            for relative in json.loads(package_index.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))['files']:
                path = (package / relative).resolve()
                if not path.is_relative_to(package.resolve()) or not path.is_file():
                    return log('Findings package file unavailable: ' + relative)

            if updated.returncode:
                return log('Findings evidence staging failed: ' + updated.stderr.strip()[-300:])
        tree = git("write-tree")

            return log("Findings tree creation failed: %s" % tree.stderr.strip()[-300:])
        tree = tree.stdout.strip()
        old_tree = git("rev-parse", parent + "^{tree}")

        if commit.returncode:
            return log("Findings commit failed: %s" % commit.stderr.strip()[-300:])
        pushed = git("push", "findings", commit.stdout.strip() + ":refs/heads/main")
        log("Findings published." if not pushed.returncode else "Findings push failed: %s" % pushed.stderr.strip()[-300:])
    finally:
        if index.exists():
            index.unlink()
